subject: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap (ClearPath)
messages:
From: Ashley Torres <ashley@clearpath.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement-clearpath@clearpath.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. As we're moving toward procurement sign-off there is one ask from our ops and legal teams we need to resolve before finalizing the PO.

ClearPath runs a recurring maintenance window (2x/month, 4 hours each) for its primary integration tests and periodic kernel updates. Because those windows are predictable and scheduled during off-peak hours, our SREs want those not to be treated as unplanned downtime for the purposes of the uptime SLA calculation.

Specifically we are asking:
- An explicit carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows (we will provide calendar invites 7 days in advance).
- A monthly service-credit cap so that a single maintenance-related incident cannot blow past our financial expectations; suggested cap: $7,500 or 15% of the monthly committed spend (whichever is lower).

Can Redwood accommodate an exception and, if so, provide proposed contract language we can include in the amendment? Procurement is targeting signature by 2026-11-12, so we'd appreciate a quick turn.

I've attached our maintenance-plan-CP-v2.pdf for context.

Best,
Ashley Torres
Sr. IT Ops Manager
ClearPath Financial

Attachment(s): maintenance-plan-CP-v2.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Ashley Torres <ashley@clearpath.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap

Ashley — thanks for the clear note and the plan. Looping in Marcus (platform/runtime) and Laura (legal) so we can give you a cohesive proposal.

Quick notes from my side:
- We generally exclude customer-scheduled maintenance when the customer controls the maintenance window and notifies us in advance. That said, we need to align on how that exclusion impacts uptime calculation across hosted vs. dedicated/private deployments.
- On the credit cap: Redwood typically ties monthly credits to a percentage of committed monthly spend for fairness. I've seen both fixed-dollar caps and percentage-based caps work depending on contract size.

Marcus / Laura — can you review Ashley's ask and propose specific language (SLA amendment) and the operational guardrails (what qualifies as a scheduled maintenance event, how to publish windows, minimum notice, blackout dates)? Also flag any risk if we add a carve-out that could be abused.

Ashley — we'll aim to send a draft amendment and SLO calculation note by EOD Wednesday. Would that timeline work for procurement?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap

Ben / Ashley — I reviewed the maintenance-plan doc. Technically we can accommodate a scheduled-maintenance exclusion but recommend the following to keep the SLA measurable and protect against excessive scheduled downtimes: 

Proposed operational rules (draft):
- Definition: "Scheduled Maintenance" = maintenance windows initiated by ClearPath where Redwood is notified at least 168 hours (7 days) in advance and a calendar invite is posted to the shared maintenance calendar.
- Maximum monthly scheduled maintenance allowance: 8 hours per calendar month (can be increased by mutual agreement in writing). Any scheduled maintenance beyond allowance counts toward downtime for SLA calculation.
- Exclusion mechanism: For uptime calculation, exclude the scheduled window only if Redwood's incident system receives the pre-notification and the maintenance window is executed during the pre-notified period.
- Emergency fixes: emergency (unplanned) maintenance requested less than 7 days' notice will not be excluded.

SLA math suggestion:
- Continue to publish the standard uptime target at 99.95% for hosted customers. For private/dedicated deployments with bespoke maintenance allowances, we can publish an amended uptime target (e.g., 99.90%) if the customer requires larger maintenance windows as part of capacity reservations.

Credit cap options (pick one):
A) Fixed-dollar cap: $5,000/month for accounts under $50k monthly committed spend; $10,000/month for larger commitments.
B) Percent cap: 10% of monthly committed spend.

I'll attach a short SLO-delta-draft.docx with sample contract language. Legal will need to review the exact phrasing.

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): slo-delta-draft.docx
From: Ashley Torres <ashley@clearpath.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement-clearpath@clearpath.com
Date: 2026-11-04T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap

Ben / Marcus — thanks for the thorough proposal. A couple of clarifications from procurement and finance: 
- The 8-hour monthly allowance works operationally, but procurement prefers a higher dollar cap to be explicit in the amendment. Their preference is $7,500/month fixed cap (we understand Redwood's A/B options but this is our ask).
- If we accept an exclusion and an allowance, how does that affect the stated uptime % in the contract? Procurement will not accept degradation of the advertised uptime (they want the same number on the face of the agreement). They want the carve-out to be clearly called out as an exception, not a lowered uptime commitment.
- Also we need a clause describing how a credit is calculated when an incident overlaps a scheduled window partially.

We are on a tight timeline for legal review — can you send redline-ready amendment language and the credit calculation example (math with sample numbers) by EOD Thursday? We'll try to push procurement to sign by 11/12 if we get that.

Thanks,
Ashley

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Ashley Torres <ashley@clearpath.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA deviation for scheduled maintenance / credit cap

Ashley — appreciate the fast feedback. Attached is a redline-ready amendment (contract-amendment-template.docx) and a short example calc we can insert into the amendment. High-level proposal to resolve both sides' concerns: 

1) Face-of-agreement uptime: remain at 99.95%.
2) Carve-out language: "Scheduled Maintenance" will be excluded from uptime calculations only when Redwood receives >=168 hours' notice and the window is published to the shared calendar. The amendment will include the 8-hour monthly allowance as Marcus suggested.
3) Credit cap: Redwood agrees to a fixed-dollar monthly cap of $6,000 for the first 12 months of the agreement. At renewal, the parties will revisit the cap; alternatively parties may elect the percent-based cap (10% of committed spend) if annual committed spend exceeds $600k.
4) Overlap calculation: credits will be prorated for periods that partially overlap scheduled windows; example: if a 2-hour downtime occurs where 30 minutes are inside an approved maintenance window and 90 minutes are outside, the credit calculation will only count the 90 minutes as eligible for SLA credit. Example calculation is included in the attached amendment.

If ClearPath can accept items 1–4 we will prepare a final PDF for signature and can expedite DocuSign routing. Requesting confirmation by 2026-11-09 to meet your procurement target.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment(s): contract-amendment-template.docx
